outcome.evidence: NO PDF PAGE READ; no decree seen, and this is the most tangled procedural history in my chunk. MARC 520$a (Bowman), quoted in full: 'Claim filed by Jose Joaquin Estudillo May 31, 1852. Confirmed by the Board Jan. 9, 1855. Confirmed by the District Court May 7, 1857, and Sept 1, 1862. Case remanded by the Supreme Court Dec. 20, 1858, by mandate, and rejected intervention on April 18, 1864. Patent issued to Jose Joaquin Estudillo July 15, 1863, for 6,829.58 acres.' Three things the register's bare 'Confirmed' hides: the Board CONFIRMED at first instance (so the concealed-reversal trap does NOT fire), but the Supreme Court REMANDED the case on 20 Dec 1858 after the first District Court confirmation, forcing a second District Court decree on 1 Sept 1862, and a separate intervention was litigated and rejected as late as 18 April 1864 - ten months AFTER the patent issued on 15 July 1863.
